The table gives the local node connectivity of every pair: A and C are joined directly and through B and through D, three routes that share no other node (accent cells), while every other pair has two." width="100%"} The local node connectivity of two nodes is the number of paths between them that share no other node: the number of other nodes that must fail to separate them, plus one if they are adjacent. This method returns it for every pair, as a table, which shows where a network is fragile in more detail than the single number of `node_connectivity()` or `average_node_connectivity()`: pairs with a value of 1 hang on a single intermediary. Pairs follow edge direction on directed graphs, so `result[u][v]` and `result[v][u]` may differ. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Only compute pairs among these nodes (IDs or labels). Paths may still pass through any node. If `None` (default), all pairs are computed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `result[u][v]` is the local node connectivity from `u` to `v`, for every ordered pair of distinct nodes (symmetric on undirected graphs). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node in `nodes=` does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each pair is one maximum flow in the auxiliary network that splits every node into an in-copy and an out-copy joined by a unit-capacity arc (Dinic's algorithm); undirected graphs solve each unordered pair once. Results match NetworkX's `all_pairs_node_connectivity()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a square `A-B-C-D` with the diagonal `A-C`, opposite corners `B` and `D` are joined through both `A` and `C`, while the diagonal's ends have three disjoint routes: ::: {#6c389fc8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec square = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A"), ("A", "C")]) ) label = square.get_label_from_id table = square.all_pairs_node_connectivity() {label(u): {label(v): k for v, k in row.items()} for u, row in table.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': {'B': 2, 'C': 3, 'D': 2}, 'B': {'A': 2, 'C': 2, 'D': 2}, 'C': {'A': 3, 'B': 2, 'D': 2}, 'D': {'A': 2, 'B': 2, 'C': 2}} ``` ::: :::
